issues.body: `attested_review_head` still loops newest-first but returns the first record whose cause is `human-arm`, silently skipping newer authenticated records with another cause. Thus history containing an older `human-arm(head=live)` followed by a newer `injection(head=live)` still returns the older head and lets `approval_coverage` produce `covers-head`, contrary to the documented `Newest receipt wins` rule. The new test matrix does not catch this: its off-cause case contains no older human-arm record, while its supersession case contains two human-arm records. Historical approval evidence therefore remains reusable across a later park episode.
issues.fix_hint: Choose the newest authenticated, well-formed park-reason record first and return its head only when that record has `cause=human-arm`; otherwise return no attestation. Add a literal end-to-end regression with an older matching human-arm receipt followed by a newer authenticated off-cause receipt, asserting it cannot render `covers-head` and cannot exit 0.
issues.title: A newer off-cause park still fails to supersede an older human-arm attestation

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-3 trust-plane defect remains unchanged. `attested_review_head` still searches backward until it finds any `human-arm` record, rather than allowing the newest authenticated park-reason record to supersede older evidence. The expanded tests cover an off-cause receipt only in isolation and newest-wins only between two `human-arm` receipts; they still omit the decisive older-human-arm/newer-off-cause sequence. Consequently a later injection or other park episode can resurrect an earlier approval binding and permit `covers-head`. This is materially the same major finding at the same severity, so progress is stagnant.
